goal: Re-investigate CTRL-003's unexplained PD/LQR run-to-run non-reproducibility with fresh eyes on the actual code
changed_files: double_pendulum_eval/scripts/run_clean_experiment.sh (PD path: replaced blind sleep 2 with an active /effort_controller/commands readiness poll)
double_pendulum_eval/run_experiment.py (_on_tick now gates the schedule clock on real /joint_states data having arrived; added a 30s startup safety timeout)

bugs_found.description: PD controller startup had no readiness check at all (blind sleep 2), unlike LQR's log-based check. A slow ROS graph discovery could leave the experiment running against a controller not yet connected to /effort_controller/commands -- zero real torque for part or all of the run.

run_experiment.py's settle/disturbance/total_duration schedule started counting from node construction (via the first _on_tick call lazily setting t0), not from real /joint_states data flow. A slow discovery could burn through the whole scenario before any sample was recorded.
bugs_found.confirmed_by: a run recording n_samples_joint_states=0, n_samples_effort=0 for a full 6s scenario despite the topic genuinely flowing (confirmed by a separate liveness check)

bugs_found.description: pkill -9 (SIGKILL) cleanup doesn't let FastRTPS release its /dev/shm shared-memory segments cleanly; they accumulate (and some corrupt) across repeated launch/kill cycles within a session, causing later RTPS_TRANSPORT_SHM open_and_lock_file failures.
bugs_found.reason_not_fixed_permanently: that shared-memory space is not scoped to this project -- it is shared by every ROS2 process at the same DOMAIN_ID on the machine, including any other concurrent session. Applied manually, one-off, for this investigation's own batches only, per explicit user direction after a real collision with another concurrent session mid-investigation.

regression_checks.single_run_clean_experiment_lqr_not_sepa: not yet done -- LQR wasn't the focus of this investigation since it already had its own (imperfect but present) readiness check; worth a follow-up spot check

notes: The 'chaotic' run-to-run variance was not genuine physics/control chaos -- it was almost entirely explained by two concrete, fixable measurement-validity bugs. With both fixed, pd/nominal_balance is highly reproducible (overshoot_q1_deg varies by at most ~0.08deg across 7 runs, not 170+). None of the 7 runs actually pass nominal_balance's acceptance criteria -- settling_time_q1_s consistently lands at 3.3-3.4s against a 3.0s max. This is now an honest, ordinary gain-tuning gap, not a reproducibility mystery. The third factor found (FastRTPS /dev/shm accumulation) is real and reproducible but deliberately not baked into the shared pipeline, since it's a machine-wide resource, not a project-scoped one -- documented as a known factor with its exact fix for anyone running this in a single-tenant environment.
